original_test_intent: Perform 250 DC reboot cycles and prove every required PCIe function returns with the correct identity and link state after each boot.

original_procedure_criteria.procedure: Run the source WAT 250-cycle scenario; title specifies `pciePoll()`.
original_procedure_criteria.criteria: All required PCIe devices remain present and healthy.

historical_reviews.v3: IMPROVED REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION with WAT mapping and complete per-BDF baseline requirements.

v3_1_conclusion.manual_test_activity: Engineer supplies package semantics, DC plan and expected topology; WAT may execute the approved cycle automatically.

master_vs_project_parameters.master_default: 250 DC cycles and a pciePoll check for all required PCIe functions.
master_vs_project_parameters.project_inputs: WAT version/token mapping, DC behavior, BDF/device/link baseline, dynamic allowlist and readiness.
master_vs_project_parameters.coverage_difference: Missing functions or reduced cycle count must be explicit.

original_method: The original WAT command and pciePoll title remain separate source facts.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use WAT only if its manual proves pciePoll coverage; compare stable BDF/vendor/device/class and link attributes instead of counts.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Signed WAT package and platform firmware required.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable WAT manual and platform PCIe topology/specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Strengthens identity/link evidence without replacing the cycle tool.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: All required functions per cycle remain required.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Count-only inventory can miss substitutions or degraded links.

safety_boundaries: No guessed scenario, hidden retry or log clearing
expected_evidence: Per-BDF identity/link and AER diff each cycle
review_improvement: KEEP: V3 already preserved the private-tool uncertainty and replaced inadequate device counts with stable per-function evidence.
